title: Parser release qualification source-recognition work record

regions.description: The three declared source regions in decoded_utf8 coordinates: header [0, body_start), body [body_start, body_end), tail [body_end, len). Derived from aozora_body_range alone and mapped back through the sanitize map. The tail is anchored on the body end, not on that function's tail start, so the blank lines between them belong to the tail rather than to no region. See docs/adr/parser-rq-source-region-partition.md.

region_interval.description: A declared region. Unlike a measurement interval this may be empty: a work with no editorial header has an empty header region and one with no colophon has an empty tail, and both are legitimate rather than defective. Endpoints share the safe-integer maximum every other offset in this protocol carries, so a region cannot describe a file no consumer could address; start <= end is NOT expressible here and is enforced by the validators, which check the whole ordered chain across all three regions rather than each region alone.

metadata.description: The metadata population: header and tail folded together. They are distinct regions so a failure localizes to one end of the file, but they qualify under one conjunctive predicate, so their totals are folded here. The measure is ATTRIBUTION and not byte accounting: a byte counts only when covered by a fact whose source_role the classified-source policy lists in metadata_attributing_roles, and a preserved_opaque fact never counts because that disposition is the statement that nothing is claimed about the bytes. A byte may therefore be accounted for by some fact and still be unattributed. TWO DENOMINATORS ARE PUBLISHED AND THE RATIO IS OVER content_bytes, NOT eligible_bytes. eligible_bytes is the header and tail regions whole, kept because it is what makes the region partition assertable: eligible_bytes + metadata.eligible_bytes == the decoded file, disjoint. content_bytes is the same regions with line terminators and wholly blank lines removed, and it is the attribution denominator. A line terminator is not packaging that can be understood or misunderstood but the delimiter between packaging items, present in identical quantity however much the instrument recognizes; counting it made the measure unreachable at 1.0 by construction and made a CRLF work score strictly below a byte-identical LF work whose packaging is understood exactly as well. A wholly blank line is excluded on the same footing, and a line of nothing but layout whitespace is excluded with it, because otherwise the measure would move according to whether a transcriber left trailing spaces.

content_bytes.description: The attribution denominator. Never greater than eligible_bytes and never less than attributed_bytes; the instrument refuses to emit a record where either fails.

unattributed_bytes.description: Region bytes carrying no attributing fact, terminators and blank lines included. Kept as the region-denominator complement.

unattributed_content_bytes.description: Content bytes carrying no attributing fact: the complement that the ratio is over, and the one that says what packaging was not understood. attributed_bytes + unattributed_content_bytes == content_bytes.

unattributed_content.description: Where the unattributed content is. This is the interval set a reader wants when asking what packaging the instrument failed to place; unattributed above is dominated by line terminators.

description: v2. eligible_bytes is the BODY region, not the whole decoded file: the ledger's facts come from lexing the body projection, so a whole-file denominator divided across a coordinate boundary. The header and tail are measured separately under `metadata`, so no byte leaves the accounting. Published v1 records are validated by parser-rq-source-recognition-work-v1.schema.json. See docs/adr/parser-rq-source-region-partition.md.
